# Vision Clipping

> Vision Clipping is a done-for-you clipping and content distribution agency. It turns long-form content into short-form clips and posts them every day across a network of TikTok, Instagram, YouTube and Facebook accounts that the client owns, run by its own team on dedicated devices, geo-targeted to the markets the client sells in, with click attribution on every post. A separate music offer places artists' songs into trending edit formats across pages Vision Clipping owns.

Key facts:
- Co-founders: Jaden Malcolm and Emrah Bayraktar. Co-founder Emrah Bayraktar has been featured in Forbes, The New York Times and NPR reporting on the clipping industry.
- Results: 3 billion+ views generated for clients.
- Clients include Red Bull, LEGO, FaZe Clan, SHEIN, WD-40, Iman Gadzhi, Luke Belmar, Russell Brunson; content cut for Sexyy Red, NLE Choppa, JoJo Siwa.
- Brand offer: One channel: $3,000/month (4 accounts, 120 posts a month, $400 one-time setup); Four channels (recommended): $12,000/month (16 accounts, 480 posts a month, $1,600 one-time setup). Three-month minimum.
- Music offer: Minimum: £1,000/month (90 posts a month, 1 song, 2 niches); Standard: £3,000/month (300 posts a month, 2 songs, 3 niches); Premium: £5,000/month (300 posts on Vision Clipping pages, 90 on the artist's own accounts, 3 accounts the artist owns); Elite: £10,000/month (450 posts on Vision Clipping pages, 270 on the artist's own accounts, 9 accounts the artist owns).
- What makes it different: Accounts are owned by the client, not rented from anonymous clippers. One team runs everything: strategy, cutting, posting and reporting. Geo-targeted distribution from devices in the client's market. Attribution on every post, so clips are judged on traffic and sales, not views alone.
- Book a call: https://vision-clipping.com/book/ · Music enquiries: https://vision-clipping.com/music/start/
- Structured facts: https://vision-clipping.com/facts.json · Full text with video transcripts: https://vision-clipping.com/llms-full.txt

## Case studies

- [Iman Gadzhi Case Study: 300M Total views, Vision Clipping](https://vision-clipping.com/cases/iman-gadzhi/): His main channels were already huge. The funnel still needed more traffic than they could produce, so we built two new accounts whose only job was click-through.
- [Luke Belmar Case Study: $102,295 Tracked revenue, Vision Clipping](https://vision-clipping.com/cases/luke-belmar/): We were paid 30% of every sale and nothing if it did not convert. Five months later the clips had sold $102,295 of a $499 product and turned him into a global meme.
- [Russell Brunson Case Study: 1M Views a month, Vision Clipping](https://vision-clipping.com/cases/russell-brunson/): A billion-dollar founder with a huge content library and no short form system. We built the whole thing from nothing and measured every clip on revenue.
- [Arab Case Study: 600.7M Total views, Vision Clipping](https://vision-clipping.com/cases/arab/): A page stuck at around 150,000 followers with no system behind it. We took over distribution in August 2025 and grew it past a million followers and 600 million views.
- [Nonstop Case Study: 676M Long form views, Vision Clipping](https://vision-clipping.com/cases/nonstop/): A basketball documentary channel built to keep earning for years. We rebuilt the storytelling from the ground up and clipped every film for social.
- [Case Studies: 3B+ Views Engineered, Vision Clipping](https://vision-clipping.com/cases/): 17 campaigns, from Russell Brunson and Iman Gadzhi to Nonstop and Sexyy Red. What we were asked to do, what we built and what it produced.
- [Global Broadcast Media Case Study: 5M+ Views generated, Vision Clipping](https://vision-clipping.com/cases/global-broadcast-media/): They messaged us three weeks before the end of the World Cup with no accounts and no infrastructure. One week later the whole operation was live.
- [Prediction Market Case Study: 13.7M First campaign views, Vision Clipping](https://vision-clipping.com/cases/prediction-markets/): A World Cup campaign to reach people who had never heard of them. 13.7 million views in three weeks, four times the web traffic, and they tripled their spend the next month.
- [WTF Games Case Study: 3.6M Views, Vision Clipping](https://vision-clipping.com/cases/wtf-games/): A content concept nobody in their space had done before, aimed at three specific countries and nowhere else. Nine accounts, each one built for one market.
- [Musa Case Study: 100K Total views, Vision Clipping](https://vision-clipping.com/cases/musa/): A founder who already knows clipping inside out wanted to see a different editing perspective on his own content. Our clips became some of the best performers on his page.
- [Dr Insanity Case Study: 18M Long form views, Vision Clipping](https://vision-clipping.com/cases/dr-insanity/): Creative direction on a flagship video that reached 18 million views, then a month of clipping on a channel that had never posted a short, right up to its acquisition.
- [Midwest Safety Case Study: 7.5M Long form views, Vision Clipping](https://vision-clipping.com/cases/midwest-safety/): One of the biggest bodycam channels on YouTube needed to publish more without dropping the quality its audience expects. We took on editing and creative direction.
- [Daniel Bitton Case Study: 1.6M Long form views, Vision Clipping](https://vision-clipping.com/cases/daniel-bitton/): He only had to film. Strategy, ideas, scripting, the team and delivery were all ours, and the most viral videos on his second channel were produced by us.
- [Evelyn Effrim-Botchey Case Study: 100K Views on top video, Vision Clipping](https://vision-clipping.com/cases/evelyn-effrim-botchey/): A brand-new personal brand that wanted to see what proper creative direction would change. Her best video yet hit 100,000 views, and Vogue noticed.
- [Sexyy Red Case Study: 4.9M Views on the trailer, Vision Clipping](https://vision-clipping.com/cases/sexyy-red/): Sexyy Red's PrankU episode needed a trailer that could stop her fans mid-scroll. We cut it from the long form episode and it went out on her own Instagram.
- [NLE Choppa Case Study: 859K Views on the trailer, Vision Clipping](https://vision-clipping.com/cases/nle-choppa/): NLE Choppa's PrankU episode needed a trailer that could stop his fans mid-scroll. We cut it from the long form episode and it went out on his own Instagram.
- [Jynxzi & Sketch Case Study: 1.5M Views on the trailer, Vision Clipping](https://vision-clipping.com/cases/jynxzi-sketch/): Jynxzi & Sketch's PrankU episode needed a trailer that could stop their fans mid-scroll. We cut it from the long form episode and it went out on their own Instagram.
- [JoJo Siwa Case Study: 577K Views on the trailer, Vision Clipping](https://vision-clipping.com/cases/jojo-siwa/): JoJo Siwa's PrankU episode needed a trailer that could stop her fans mid-scroll. We cut it from the long form episode and it went out on her own Instagram.

## Breakdowns (cited analysis of clipping campaigns)

- [Breakdowns: How the Big Names Actually Distribute | Vision Clipping](https://vision-clipping.com/breakdowns/): Cited breakdowns of how big creators, brands and platforms really run clipping and short-form distribution, and what we would do differently.
- [Inside Iman Gadzhi's Clipping Operation](https://vision-clipping.com/breakdowns/iman-gadzhi-clipping/): Iman Gadzhi's Instagram has posted about a hundred times. The machine reposting him has posted thousands. How his clipping operation works, what it costs, where it breaks, and the controlled version.
- [Luke Belmar Stopped Posting in 2023. The Clipping Machine Didn't.](https://vision-clipping.com/breakdowns/luke-belmar-clipping/): Luke Belmar has uploaded ten YouTube videos in his life, the last in September 2023. His reach lives in podcast appearances and a swarm of clip pages. A cited breakdown of the most rented audience in the creator economy.
- [Inside Polymarket's Clipping Campaign: 140 Million Views, Then the Consequences](https://vision-clipping.com/breakdowns/polymarket-clipping/): Polymarket bought 140 million views from per-view clippers at $0.50 to $1 per thousand. Then came the WSJ analysis, a lawsuit and two senators. A cited breakdown of the cheapest reach in marketing.
- [How Music Labels Quietly Pay to Make Songs Go Viral](https://vision-clipping.com/breakdowns/music-clipping/): A major-label marketer estimates 75% of popular TikTok songs started as paid creator campaigns. The rate card, the burner accounts, the sped-up flywheel and the disclosure gray zone, cited.
- [How Diary of a CEO Mastered Podcast Clipping](https://vision-clipping.com/breakdowns/diary-of-a-ceo-clipping/): How Diary of a CEO mastered podcast clipping: moments flagged mid-interview, thumbnails tested as Facebook ads, 150 experiments a quarter, and how to make clips like DOAC yourself. Cited.
- [Did Andrew Tate Invent Clipping? Inside the Campaign That Built an Industry](https://vision-clipping.com/breakdowns/andrew-tate-clipping/): The Andrew Tate clipping campaign, explained: Hustler's University paid commissions to flood TikTok with his most controversial clips, 11.6 billion views by August 2022, and a playbook the whole industry copied. Cited.
- [The Joe Rogan Clip Economy: Half of the Biggest Podcast's Views Are Clips](https://vision-clipping.com/breakdowns/joe-rogan-clips/): Joe Rogan's official clips channel has 6 billion views, roughly half of all official JRE YouTube views ever. Why clips stayed on YouTube through the Spotify deal, and what the Trump episode proved. Cited.
- [How Stake Built Gambling's Viral Clipping Machine](https://vision-clipping.com/breakdowns/stake-clipping/): Barred from normal advertising, Stake grew to $4.7B in revenue on a three-layer machine: its own streaming platform, nine-figure star deals, and clippers paid as little as two cents per thousand views. Cited.

- [Mass Clipping Campaign vs Internal Clipping Campaign](https://vision-clipping.com/blog/mass-clipping-campaign-vs-internal-clipping-campaign/): Mass clipping campaigns versus internal, owned-account clipping compared on cost, ownership, control, attribution and risk, plus how to choose the right one for your brand.
- [Why You Should Build Your Clipping Team In-House](https://vision-clipping.com/blog/why-build-your-clipping-team-in-house/): The case for running clipping in-house: you own the accounts, control quality and targeting, and build an asset. Plus the real cost, and the managed way to get it without hiring.
- [Why You Should Do Mass Clipping](https://vision-clipping.com/blog/why-you-should-do-mass-clipping/): The case for mass clipping: cheap reach at huge scale, fast, and great for launches. Plus when it works, the pitfalls to avoid, and how to run it without getting botted.
- [Is clipping a "weapon of mass manipulation"? What Le Monde found](https://vision-clipping.com/blog/is-clipping-mass-manipulation/): Le Monde called clipping the internet's new weapon of mass manipulation. Here is what France's paper of record got right about the scale, where the real risk actually sits, and how legitimate clipping for brands is different.
